threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 149 bus is a reliable way to get home after 10 PM. Welcome to Dalston, mate, good luck with that!
Last night on the 59, a man pulled out a whole roast chicken from his bag and shared it with the driver. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I stumbled upon that hidden café on a side street, its walls covered in local art and the smell of fresh bread wafting out. Never knew such gems existed.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you sip a beer while watching a public art protest on the same corner where kids are playing hopscotch. It's a wild mix.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they dodge tourists on Valencia without breaking stride—those city slickers don't even glance up from their phones.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy offer his seat to a toddler on Muni today; the kid just blinked and stared—sanctuary city moment in a hectic commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals love loud street parties, but many of us just want a quiet evening with a book, especially after a week of extra noise.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them easily; they’re the ones still holding a map upside down while navigating the Plaça del Sol.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the bus will come when it says on the screen. The real London timing has a mind of its own, mate.
Caught a night bus from Brixton the other week; a guy argued with the driver over the last donut from a nearby kebab shop.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw someone using a bike as a stroller for their dog outside the Späti at 2 AM. That’s classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do people celebrate a bus strike with picnics on the roads, making the most of transit chaos like it’s a public holiday.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you’re from the Mission when you can spot a tourist by their confused expression at the BART delays. They think it’s just a bad day.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy with a full keyboard on a Muni bus, playing tunes to a captive crowd. Only in SF does that feel like a regular Tuesday.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists flock to Park Güell but miss the real charm of Gràcia's hidden squares, where locals sip vermut and chat for hours, completely overlooked.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re still trying to make sense of the metro map—look for the ones squinting and flipping it upside down at the station.
